relevance_reason: Reports a germline MYH11 frameshift mutation in one individual with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, with functional evidence of an unregulated, constitutively active myosin; relevant as possible additional genetic contribution to PJS.

findings.statement: Alhopuro et al. (2008) screened patients with colorectal cancer, Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS), and juvenile polyposis for MYH11 mutations, prompted by the zebrafish meltdown (mlt) mutant, which carries a recessive ATPase-activating smooth-muscle myosin mutation and develops intestinal abnormalities reminiscent of PJS and juvenile polyposis. They found a germline protein-elongating frameshift mutation in MYH11 in one individual with PJS.
quotes: The mlt zebrafish develops intestinal abnormalities reminiscent of human Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) and juvenile polyposis (JP).
We found somatic protein-elongating frameshift mutations in 55% of CRCs displaying microsatellite instability and in the germ-line of one individual with PJS.

findings.statement: Alhopuro et al. (2008) functionally evaluated the MYH11 frameshift mutations and found that they resulted in unregulated myosin molecules displaying constitutive motor activity, similar to the mutant myosin underlying the zebrafish mlt phenotype. They suggested that unregulated MYH11 may affect cellular energy balance or disturb cell lineage decisions in tumor progenitor cells, and that MYH11 mutations appear to contribute to human intestinal neoplasia.
quotes: All mutations resulted in unregulated molecules displaying constitutive motor activity, similar to the mutant myosin underlying mlt.
Unregulated MYH11 may affect the cellular energy balance or disturb cell lineage decisions in tumor progenitor cells.

findings.statement: In 2 sibs with PJS and primary gastric cancer, Shinmura et al. (2005) identified a novel germline STK11 mutation, c.890delG, predicted to encode a truncated protein (p.Arg297fsX38), by sequencing. No germline mutations in CDH1 or TP53 were detected. No inactivation of the wildtype STK11 allele by somatic mutation, chromosomal deletion, or 5-prime CpG hypermethylation was detected in the gastric cancer.
quotes: A novel type of the STK11 germline mutation, c.890delG, encoding a truncated protein (p.Arg297fsX38) was identified, but no germline mutations of the CDH1 and TP53 genes were detected.
No inactivation of the wild-type allele by somatic mutation or chromosomal deletion or hypermethylation at the 5'-CpG site of STK11 was detected in the GC.

relevance_reason: Reports a de novo germline STK11/LKB1 truncating mutation in a simplex PJS patient and LOH studies of the patient's hamartomatous polyps.

findings.statement: Hernan et al. (2004) identified a de novo heterozygous germline mutation in exon 6 of the STK11/LKB1 gene in a simplex case of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. The mutation was described as a substitution of cytosine for guanine at codon 246, resulting in a premature stop codon (Tyr246X). The authors predicted that it would produce a truncated protein with presumed loss of kinase activity. The mutation was not found in either parent.
quotes: Molecular analysis of the LKB1 gene in a simplex case of PJS revealed a substitution of cytosine (C) for guanine (G) at codon 246 in exon 6, resulting in the Tyr246X mutation.
The nucleotide substitution leads to a premature stop codon at the 246 residue, predicting a truncated protein and presumed loss of kinase activity.
Analysis of DNA from both parents of the PJS patient did not show this mutation, which is therefore a de novo mutation.

findings.statement: Hernan et al. (2004) used real-time fluorescence PCR genotyping with fluorescent resonance energy transfer to study loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus. They used DNA from microdissected gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps from a PJS patient with a de novo Tyr246X mutation. The results suggested that hamartomatous polyps form by a mechanism other than LOH.
quotes: We isolated DNA from microdissected gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps in the PJS patient and investigated the loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus by real-time fluorescence polymerase chain reaction genotyping using a fluorescent resonance energy transfer technique.
The results suggest a different mechanism from LOH in the formation of hamartomatous polyps.

relevance_reason: Reports STK11 mutation detection rates, clinical onset data and genotype-phenotype correlations in a PJS cohort.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2004) characterized STK11 mutations in 42 independent probands and detected mutations in 22 of 32 (69%) probands with PJS and in none of 10 probands referred to rule out PJS. Real-time PCR quantitation of DNA failed to detect large deletions in PJS participants without STK11 mutations. The authors concluded that direct sequencing of STK11 yields a high rate of point mutations in individuals who meet phenotypic PJS criteria.
quotes: Mutations were detected in 22/32 (69%) probands with PJS and 0/10 probands referred to rule out PJS.
Real-time PCR analysis to quantitate DNA failed to detect any large deletions in PJS participants without STK11 mutations.
Direct sequencing of STK11 yields a high rate of point mutations in individuals who meet phenotypic PJS criteria.

findings.statement: In a historical cohort of 51 individuals with PJS who completed self-administered questionnaires, Amos et al. (2004) found a median time to onset of gastrointestinal symptoms or polypectomy of 13 years, with wide variability. Gastric polyps were frequent, with a median age at onset of 16 years; the authors suggested that the common occurrence of gastric polyps may facilitate chemopreventive studies.
quotes: The median time to onset for gastrointestinal symptoms or polypectomy was 13 years of age but showed a wide variability.
Gastric polyps were frequent in PJS participants, with a median age at onset of 16 years.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2004) found that individuals with missense mutations in STK11 had a significantly later time to onset of first polypectomy (p = 0.04) and of other symptoms compared with those with truncating mutations or no detectable mutation.
quotes: Individuals with missense mutations had a significantly later time to onset of first polypectomy (p = 0.04) and of other symptoms compared with those participants either with truncating mutations or no detectable mutation.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2004) concluded that STK11 mutation analysis should be restricted to individuals who meet PJS criteria or their close relatives.
quotes: STK11 mutation analysis should be restricted to individuals who meet PJS criteria or their close relatives.

relevance_reason: Reports a PJS family with a complete germline heterozygous deletion of STK11, establishing large deletions as a mutation mechanism.

findings.statement: Le Meur et al. (2004) reported a family with typical features of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, including gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps, breast cancers, and melanin spots of the oral mucosa.
quotes: We report the case of a family with typical features of PJS, including gastrointestinal hamartomatous, breast cancers and melanin spots of the oral mucosa.

phenotypes.text: melanin spots of the oral mucosa

findings.statement: In a family with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, Le Meur et al. (2004) used quantitative multiplex PCR of short fluorescent fragments (QMPSF) of the 19p13 region to identify an approximately 250-kb heterozygous germline deletion removing the entire STK11 locus. They stated this was the first description of a complete germline deletion of STK11 and suggested that large genomic deletions should be considered in PJS families without detectable STK11 point mutations.
quotes: Quantitative multiplex PCR of short fluorescent fragments (QMPSF) of the 19p13 region allowed us to identify an approximately 250 kb heterozygous deletion removing entirely the STK11 locus.

This report, which constitutes the first description of a complete germline deletion of STK11, shows that the presence of such large genomic deletions should be considered in PJS families without detectable point mutations of STK11.

variants.as_reported: approximately 250 kb heterozygous deletion removing entirely the STK11 locus

findings.statement: Le Meur et al. (2004) noted that detection of STK11 germline mutations in only 50 to 70% of PJS families had suggested genetic heterogeneity, but their finding of a complete STK11 deletion indicated that large genomic deletions may account for some mutation-negative families.
quotes: The detection of STK11 germline mutations, in only 50-70% of PJS families, has suggested a genetic heterogeneity of the disease.

relevance_reason: Excludes candidate genes for a putative second PJS locus on 19q13.3-q13.4 and STK11IP in a non-STK11 PJS family; relevant to heterogeneity/mapping.

findings.statement: Buchet-Poyau et al. (2002) noted that STK11 mutations cannot be detected in a considerable number of PJS patients, suggesting genetic heterogeneity. They studied PJS07, a family without STK11 mutations in which multipoint linkage analysis had previously given significant LOD scores for a second potential PJS locus on 19q13.3-q13.4, between markers D19S180 and D19S254.
quotes: in a considerable number of PJS-patients mutations cannot be detected in STK11 suggesting genetic heterogeneity
One PJS family without STK11 mutations (PJS07) has previously been described with significant evidence for linkage to a second potential PJS locus on 19q13.3-->q13.4.
we investigated candidate genes within markers D19S180 and D19S254, since multipoint linkage analysis yielded significant LOD scores for this region in this family

findings.statement: In the PJS07 family, Buchet-Poyau et al. (2002) screened all exons and exon-intron junctions of 4 candidate genes in the 19q13.3-q13.4 region: PSCD2, KLK10, PRKCG, and STK13. They first determined the genomic structure of PSCD2 and PRKCG. No pathogenic mutation was found in affected individuals; the only change was a very rare polymorphism in PSCD2 causing a conserved Lys-to-Arg substitution. The authors concluded that these 4 genes were excluded as candidates for the second PJS locus.
quotes: We first determined the genomic structure of the PSCD2 and PRKCG genes, and performed mutation analysis of all exons and exon-intron junctions of the four genes, in the PJS07 family.
No pathogenic mutation was identified in these four genes in affected individuals. A very rare polymorphism resulting in a conserved amino acid change Lys to Arg was found in PSCD2.
These data provide considerable evidence for exclusion of these four genes as candidates for the second locus on 19q13.3-->q13.4 in PJS.

findings.statement: Buchet-Poyau et al. (2002) also excluded the STK11-interacting protein gene STK11IP (LIP1), which maps to 2q36, as a candidate for PJS in the PJS07 family. They noted that it could still be a good candidate in other families without STK11 mutations.
quotes: we also excluded the recently identified STK11-interacting protein gene (STK11IP, alias LIP1) mapped in 2q36 as candidate for PJS in the PJS07 family, although this could be a good candidate in other non-STK11/LKB1 families.

quotes: Molecular genetic evidence of an association between nasal polyposis and the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

relevance_reason: The paper looks at STK11/LKB1 in 34 PJS families. It reports evidence for genetic heterogeneity and a cancer risk that differs by mutation status.

findings.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) analyzed the STK11/LKB1 locus in 34 Peutz-Jeghers syndrome families. They searched the coding sequence for mutations and rearrangements and also used allele-specific expression tests and linkage studies. They found germline deleterious STK11/LKB1 mutations in 70% of cases.
quotes: We report here the analysis of the STK11/LKB1 locus in a series of 34 PJS families, combining the search for mutations and rearrangements in the coding sequence, allele specific expression tests, and linkage studies.
Germline deleterious mutation of the STK11/LKB1 gene were identified in 70% of cases.

findings.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) found that their results strengthened the hypothesis of a second PJS locus. PJS families fell into two groups depending on whether an STK11/LKB1 alteration had been identified. The authors concluded that up to 30% of PJS patients have the disorder because of mutation in an unidentified gene.
quotes: The hypothesis of a second PJS locus was reinforced and PJS families could be divided into two groups on the basis of the presence or absence of an identified STK11/LKB1 alteration.
Up to 30% of PJS patients are caused by mutation in an unidentified gene that confers high susceptibility to cancer development.

findings.statement: Olschwang et al. (2001) found that cancer risk differed markedly between PJS families with and without an identified STK11/LKB1 mutation. PJS patients without an identified STK11/LKB1 mutation were at major risk for proximal biliary adenocarcinoma, which is an infrequent tumor in the general population.
quotes: Analysis of clinical data indicates that the cancer associated risk is markedly different in the two groups.
PJS patients with no identified STK11/LKB1 mutation are at major risk for proximal biliary adenocarcinoma, an infrequent tumour in the general population.

relevance_reason: Molecular analysis of PJS polyps and carcinomas showing 19p LOH (STK11 locus), supporting a tumor suppressor role and a distinct carcinogenesis pathway.

findings.statement: Entius et al. (2001) analyzed 39 polyps and 5 carcinomas from 17 patients from 13 families with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome for loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at 19p13.3 (the STK11/LKB1 locus). LOH at 19p was found in 15 of the 39 polyps and in all 5 carcinomas; 6 of 7 polyps from patients with cancer had LOH compared with 9 of 31 polyps from the other patients (p = 0.01). The authors concluded that STK11/LKB1 acts as a tumor suppressor gene and may be involved in the early stages of PJS tumorigenesis, and that further research was needed to see whether LOH in PJS polyps could be used as a biomarker to predict cancer.
quotes: LOH at 19p was seen in 15 of the 39 polyps and in all carcinomas (n = 5). Interestingly, six of the seven polyps from patients with cancer had LOH, compared with nine of the 31 polyps from the remaining patients (p = 0.01).
These results provide further evidence that STK11/LKB1 acts as a tumour suppressor gene, and may be involved in the early stages of PJS tumorigenesis.
Thirty nine polyps and five carcinomas from 17 patients (from 13 families) with PJS were analysed for loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at 19p13.3 (STK11/LKB1 gene locus)

findings.statement: Entius et al. (2001) found that a polyp from a PJS patient without a germline STK11/LKB1 mutation showed no LOH at 19p or at 3 alternative PJS candidate loci (19q, 6p, and 6q).
quotes: In one polyp from a patient without a germline STK11/LKB1 mutation, no LOH at 19p or at three alternative PJS candidate loci (19q, 6p, and 6q) was found.

findings.statement: Entius et al. (2001) found no LOH at 5q (APC) in PJS polyps or carcinomas, but APC mutations were found in 4 of 5 carcinomas. No 17p LOH was seen and no p53 mutation was found, although p53 immunostaining was present in 1 carcinoma and focally in 3 polyps; 1 carcinoma had an activating K-ras codon 12 mutation and another showed 18q LOH without loss of SMAD4 expression. The authors suggested that differences from the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence indicate a distinct pathway of carcinogenesis in PJS.
quotes: No LOH at 5q was observed. However, mutational analysis revealed an APC mutation in four of the five carcinomas.
One carcinoma had an activating K-ras codon 12 mutation and another carcinoma showed 18q LOH; however, no loss of Smad4 expression was seen.
Differences in molecular genetic alterations noted between the adenoma-carcinoma sequence and PJS related tumours suggest the presence of a distinct pathway of carcinogenesis.

relevance_reason: Somatic second-hit LKB1 mutations/LOH and beta-catenin/p53 changes in PJS hamartomatous polyps support the pathogenesis of PJS.

findings.statement: Miyaki et al. (2000) studied 27 gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps from 10 patients in 9 PJS families and found germline LKB1 mutations in 6 families. Somatic LKB1 mutations were found in 5 polyps, and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus on 19p was seen in 14 other polyps.
quotes: We examined mutations of the LKB1, beta-catenin, APC, K-ras, and p53 genes in 27 gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps from 10 patients in nine PJS families.

Germ-line mutations of the LKB1 gene were detected in six PJS families. Somatic mutations of the LKB1 gene were found in 5 polyps, whereas loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the LKB1 locus at 19p was seen in 14 other polyps.

findings.statement: Miyaki et al. (2000) suggested that gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps in PJS develop through inactivation of LKB1 by a germline mutation plus somatic mutation or LOH of the unaffected allele. Additional mutations of beta-catenin and p53 were suggested to convert hamartomatous polyps into adenomatous and carcinomatous lesions. Adenomatous lesions microdissected from hamartomatous polyps had both a beta-catenin mutation and 19p LOH. A carcinomatous lesion in a gastric hamartomatous polyp had a p53 mutation and LOH at the p53 locus in addition to LKB1 LOH and a beta-catenin mutation. K-ras mutations were found in a few polyps, but no APC mutations or 5q LOH were found.
quotes: These results suggest that gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps in PJS patients develop through inactivation of the LKB1 gene by germ-line mutation plus somatic mutation or LOH of the unaffected LKB1 allele, and that additional mutations of the beta-catenin gene and p53 gene convert hamartomatous polyps into adenomatous and carcinomatous lesions.
In adenomatous lesions microdissected from hamartomatous polyps, both beta-catenin mutation and 19p LOH were detected.
K-ras mutations were detected in a few polyps, whereas no APC mutation or 5q LOH was detected in hamartomatous polyps.

relevance_reason: Mutation screening of LKB1 in familial and sporadic PJS; low detection rate suggests genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Boardman et al. (2000) screened LKB1 for mutations in 5 PJS kindreds with more than 2 affected members, 5 probands with only 1 other affected relative, and 23 individuals with sporadic PJS, using conformation-sensitive gel electrophoresis, direct sequencing, and long-range PCR for larger insertions or deletions. LKB1 mutations were found in only 2 probands with a family history of PJS and in 4 of 23 sporadic cases. The authors suggested significant genetic heterogeneity for PJS and the involvement of other loci.
quotes: we evaluated five kindreds with greater than two affected family members, five PJS probands with only one other affected family member, as well as 23 individuals with sporadic PJS for mutations within the LKB1 gene
Mutation analysis revealed genetic alterations in LKB1 in two probands who had a family history of PJS. LKB1 mutations were detected in only four of the remaining 23 cases of sporadic PJS.
These data suggest the presence of significant genetic heterogeneity for PJS and the involvement of other loci in this syndrome.

findings.statement: Boardman et al. (2000) found LKB1 mutations in 6 of 33 PJS probands studied: 2 of 10 probands with a family history of PJS and 4 of 23 individuals with sporadic PJS.
quotes: Mutation analysis revealed genetic alterations in LKB1 in two probands who had a family history of PJS. LKB1 mutations were detected in only four of the remaining 23 cases of sporadic PJS.

quotes: We present a prepubertal boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, gynecomastia and bilateral neoplastic Sertoli cell proliferation

findings.statement: In the prepubertal boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, gynecomastia, and bilateral Sertoli cell proliferation, Bergadá et al. (2000) found that the only abnormal hormonal finding was increased serum concentrations of inhibin B and Pro-alpha C. They noted that gynecomastia in boys with PJS and Sertoli cell tumors results from increased estrogen production due to increased aromatase activity within the testicular tumor.
quotes: the only abnormal hormonal profile was increased concentration of inhibin B and Pro-alpha C in serum
Gynecomastia in boys with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and Sertoli cell tumors of gonadal origin results from increased estrogen production due to increased aromatase activity within the testicular tumor.

findings.statement: Jiang et al. (1999) screened 10 unrelated families with PJS for germline STK11 changes, using the protein truncation test and genomic DNA sequencing. They found a novel truncating deletion covering STK11 exons 2 through 7 in a single patient, as well as several known polymorphisms.
quotes: We conducted a detailed investigation of germline STK11 alterations by protein truncation test and genomic DNA sequence analysis in ten unrelated PJS families.
We identified a novel truncating deletion spanning STK11 exons 2-7 in a single patient and several known polymorphisms.

findings.statement: Jiang et al. (1999) studied loss of heterozygosity in PJS polyps from 4 patients and found an allelic deletion of D19S886 in a patient other than the one carrying the STK11 deletion. Because germline STK11 mutations were found in only 1 of 10 families, the authors suggested that STK11 mutations account for only a proportion of PJS cases.
quotes: Loss of heterozygosity studies in PJS polyps of four of these patients identified an allelic deletion of D19S886 in another patient.
Our results suggest that STK11 mutations account for only a proportion of PJS cases.

findings.statement: In a review, Westerman and Wilson (1999) noted that the risks from polyps in PJS patients include surgical emergencies such as small bowel intussusception, and chronic or acute bleeding from the polyps.

melanin pigmentation of skin and mucous membranes

findings.statement: Westerman and Wilson (1999) reviewed reports suggesting that PJS is associated with both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal tumours. It was not clear whether these cancers arise from the polyps. The authors suggested that the frequent occurrence of rare extraintestinal cancers points to a general susceptibility to cancer. These include sex cord tumours with annular tubules of the ovary, adenoma malignum of the cervix, and Sertoli cell tumours of the testis.
quotes: more and more reports suggest an association of PJS with both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal tumours

the frequent occurrence of some rare extra-intestinal malignancies such as tumours of the ovary (sex cord tumours with annular tubules), cervix (adenoma malignum) and testis (Sertoli cell tumours) indicates a general susceptibility for the development of malignancies

phenotypes.text: ovarian sex cord tumour with annular tubules

findings.statement: Westerman and Wilson (1999) noted that the PJS gene had recently been identified as encoding the serine threonine kinase STK11. Because of the general susceptibility to cancer in PJS, they stated that the gene is thought to act as a tumour suppressor.
quotes: The PJS gene, which was recently identified to encode for the serine threonine kinase STK11, is therefore thought to act as a tumour-suppressor gene.

findings.statement: Westerman and Wilson (1999) concluded that people who carry the PJS gene are at increased risk of cancer both inside and outside the gastrointestinal tract. As genetic identification of carriers without symptoms becomes possible, they said surveillance and screening protocols need to be developed for patients and their relatives.
quotes: PJS gene carriers not only run risks of polyp-induced gastrointestinal complications, but also are at increased risk of developing cancer, both within and outside the gastrointestinal tract.
surveillance and screening protocols need to be developed for PJS patients and their relatives

relevance_reason: Reports novel STK11 mutations in Dutch PJS families and evidence for locus heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) performed mutation analysis of LKB1/STK11 in 19 predominantly Dutch PJS families and identified 12 novel mutations in 12 families: 1 nonsense mutation, 3 frameshift deletions, 3 frameshift insertions, 2 acceptor splice site mutations, and 3 missense mutations. None of the mutations occurred in more than one family, and a number were shown to have arisen de novo. Four polymorphisms were also detected.
quotes: In 12 of these families, we identified LKB1/STK11 mutations, none of which has been described before.
These 12 novel LKB1/STK11 mutations consist of one nonsense mutation, three frameshift deletions, three frameshift insertions, two acceptor splice site mutations, and three missense mutations.
None of the mutations occurred in more than one family, and a number were demonstrated to have arisen de novo.

findings.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) found no apparent abnormalities of the LKB1/STK11 gene in 7 of 19 PJS families, which they suggested could reflect locus heterogeneity in PJS.
quotes: In the remaining seven PJS families, we found no apparent abnormalities of the LKB1/STK1I gene, which could reflect the existence of locus heterogeneity in PJS.

findings.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) noted that the diverse array of mutations, apparent high mutation rate, and possible second PJS locus make diagnostic or predictive genetic testing in individual patients difficult.
quotes: The diverse array of mutations found, the apparent high mutation rate, as well as the existence of a possible second PJS locus, renders diagnostic or predictive genetic testing in individual patients difficult

relevance_reason: Follow-up of the original Peutz family with PJS, giving clinical natural history and the LKB1 mutation that cosegregates with the disease.

findings.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) reported a follow-up of more than 78 years of the original Dutch family described by Peutz in 1921. They studied the natural history of PJS across 6 generations using interviews, physical examination, chart review and histologic review. Clinical features included gastrointestinal polyposis, mucocutaneous pigmentation, nasal polyposis and rectal extrusion of polyps. Intestinal obstruction and the development of malignant disease reduced the survival of affected family members, and the authors suggested that PJS is not a benign disease.
quotes: Clinical features in this family included gastrointestinal polyposis, mucocutaneous pigmentation, nasal polyposis, and rectal extrusion of polyps.
Survival of affected family members was reduced by intestinal obstruction and by the development of malignant disease.
The morbidity and mortality in this family suggest that PJS is not a benign disease.

findings.statement: In the original Dutch PJS family first described by Peutz, Westerman et al. (1999) identified a novel germline mutation in the LKB1 gene that cosegregated with the disease. The mutation was a T insertion at codon 66 in exon 1, which caused a frameshift and a stop at codon 162 in exon 4. The authors concluded that an inactivating germline LKB1 mutation is involved in the PJS phenotype in this, the oldest known affected kindred.
quotes: A novel germline mutation in the LKB1 gene was found to cosegregate with the disease phenotype in the original family.
The mutant LKB1 allele carried a T insertion at codon 66 in exon 1 resulting in frameshift and stop at codon 162 in exon 4.
An inactivating germline mutation in the LKB1 gene is involved in the PJS phenotype in the original and oldest kindred known to be affected by PJS.

variants.as_reported: T insertion at codon 66 in exon 1 resulting in frameshift and stop at codon 162 in exon 4

findings.statement: Westerman et al. (1999) noted that Peutz first recognized the association of heredity, gastrointestinal polyposis and mucocutaneous pigmentation in a Dutch family in 1921.
quotes: The association between heredity, gastrointestinal polyposis, and mucocutaneous pigmentation in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) was first recognised in 1921 by Peutz in a Dutch family.

relevance_reason: The study reports STK11 germline mutations in PJS families, including the original Jeghers family, and analyses the somatic pathogenesis of hamartomas and adenocarcinomas in PJS.

findings.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) studied 6 PJS families from the Johns Hopkins Polyposis Registry, including the family originally described by Jeghers in 1949. Linkage analysis confirmed linkage to 19p13.3, near the STK11 gene.
quotes: Linkage analysis in the family originally described by Jeghers in 1949 and five other families confirmed linkage to 19p13.3 near a recently identified gene responsible for PJS.

findings.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) sequenced genomic DNA and identified germline STK11 mutations in all 6 PJS families studied, including the original Jeghers family.
quotes: Germ-line mutations in this gene, STK11, were identified in all six families by sequencing genomic DNA.

findings.statement: In hamartomas and adenocarcinomas from PJS patients, Gruber et al. (1998) found loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of 19p markers near STK11 in 70% of tumors. Haplotype analysis showed that the retained allele carried the germline mutation, which the authors said confirmed that STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene. They concluded that STK11 acts as an early gatekeeper regulating hamartoma development and suggested that hamartomas may be precursors of adenocarcinoma.
quotes: Analysis of hamartomas and adenocarcinomas from patients with PJS identified loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of 19p markers near STK11 in 70% of tumors.
Haplotype analysis indicated that the retained allele carried a germ-line mutation, confirming that STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene.
STK11 is a tumor suppressor gene that acts as an early gatekeeper regulating the development of hamartomas in PJS and suggest that hamartomas may be pathogenetic precursors of adenocarcinoma

findings.statement: Gruber et al. (1998) found LOH of 17p and 18q in an adenocarcinoma but not in hamartomas, which they took to mean these are late events in PJS cancer progression. The adenocarcinomas with 17p LOH also showed altered p53 on immunohistochemistry. None of the 18 PJS tumors showed microsatellite instability, LOH on 5q near APC, or mutations in K-ras codons 12 or 13.
quotes: LOH of 17p and 18q was identified in an adenocarcinoma but not in hamartomas, implying that allelic loss of these two regions corresponds to late molecular events in the pathogenesis of cancer in PJS.
The adenocarcinomas showing 17p LOH also demonstrated altered p53 by immunohistochemistry.
None of the 18 PJS tumors showed microsatellite instability, LOH on 5q near APC, or mutations in codons 12 or 13 of the K-ras proto-oncogene.

relevance_reason: The paper reports new LKB1 (STK11) mutations in families with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, shows that the mutant proteins lose kinase activity, and gives evidence for locus heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) screened 9 PJS families of American, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Turkish, and Indian origin for LKB1 mutations and found 7 novel mutations: 2 frameshift mutations, 1 four-amino-acid deletion, 2 amino acid substitutions, and 2 splicing errors.
quotes: we screened for LKB1 mutations in nine PJS families of American, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Turkish, and Indian origin and detected seven novel mutations
These included two frameshift mutations, one four-amino-acid deletion, two amino-acid substitutions, and two splicing errors.
findings.population: American, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Turkish, Indian

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) expressed the mutant LKB1 proteins K78I, D176N, W308C, and L67P. All 4 mutants had lost autophosphorylation (kinase) activity. The authors concluded that loss of LKB1 kinase activity is probably responsible for the PJS phenotypes.
quotes: Expression of mutant LKB1 proteins (K78I, D176N, W308C, and L67P) and assessment of their autophosphorylation activity revealed a loss of the kinase activity in all of these mutants.
These results provide direct evidence that the elimination of the kinase activity of LKB1 is probably responsible for the development of the PJS phenotypes.

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) found no LKB1 mutation in 2 Indian PJS families. They had previously found linkage to markers on 19q13.3-q13.4 in one of these families, which suggested locus heterogeneity in PJS.
quotes: In two Indian families, we failed to detect any LKB1 mutation; in one of these families, we previously had detected linkage to markers on 19q13.3-4, which suggests locus heterogeneity of PJS.

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1998) described PJS as an autosomal dominant disease with mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyps, and with an increased risk of benign and malignant tumors in the gastrointestinal tract and in tissues outside it.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an autosomal dominant disease characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyps.
There is an increased risk of benign and malignant tumors in the gastrointestinal tract and in extraintestinal tissues.

relevance_reason: Reports treatment of the mucocutaneous lentigines of PJS with ruby laser in two children. This is relevant to the clinical management section.

findings.statement: Kato et al. (1998) used ruby laser therapy to treat labial lentigines in 2 children with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. The response was excellent, and the lesions did not recur and left no sequelae. The authors suggested that ruby laser therapy is safe and suitable for treating labial lentigines in children with PJS.
quotes: We describe ruby laser therapy of labial lentigines in two children with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. The response to treatment was excellent and no sequelae or recurrence of the lesions was noted.
Our experience suggests that ruby laser therapy is safe and a suitable approach for the treatment of labial lentigines in children with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

relevance_reason: Linkage study of PJS families supporting a major locus at 19p13.3 and providing evidence of genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Olschwang et al. (1998) analyzed 20 further families with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, beyond the 12 families previously found to be compatible with linkage to marker D19S886, and found that most were consistent with a PJS gene on 19p13.3. They concluded that chromosome 19p13.3 holds a major PJS locus.
quotes: We have analysed 20 further families and found that the majority of these are consistent with a PJS gene on 19p13.3.
There appears, therefore, to be a major PJS locus on chromosome 19p13.3

findings.statement: Olschwang et al. (1998) found that 3 of 20 Peutz-Jeghers syndrome families were unlinked to 19p13.3, and none of the available PJS polyps from these families showed allele loss at D19S886. The linked and unlinked families showed no obvious clinicopathologic or ethnic differences. The authors suggested that there may be a minor PJS locus (or loci) elsewhere in the genome.
quotes: Three families were, however, unlinked to 19p13.3 and none of the available PJS polyps from these families showed allele loss at D19S886.
There were no obvious clinicopathological or ethnic differences between the 19p13.3 linked and unlinked families.
the possibility exists of a minor locus (or loci) elsewhere.

relevance_reason: Landmark paper identifying truncating germline LKB1 (STK11) mutations as the cause of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) found truncating germline mutations in LKB1, a gene on chromosome 19p, in multiple individuals with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. They concluded that PJS was the first cancer-susceptibility syndrome found to be caused by inactivating mutations in a protein kinase.
quotes: We have identified truncating germline mutations in a gene residing on chromosome 19p in multiple individuals affected by PJS.
Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is therefore the first cancer-susceptibility syndrome to be identified that is due to inactivating mutations in a protein kinase.

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as a rare hereditary disease that predisposes to benign and malignant tumors in many organ systems.
quotes: the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS), a rare hereditary disease in which there is predisposition to benign and malignant tumours of many organ systems

phenotypes.text: predisposition to benign and malignant tumors of many organ systems

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1998) reported that LKB1, a gene that had already been identified but not mapped, is strongly homologous to XEEK1, a cytoplasmic serine/threonine protein kinase from Xenopus, and more weakly similar to many other protein kinases.
quotes: This previously identified but unmapped gene, LKB1, has strong homology to a cytoplasmic Xenopus serine/threonine protein kinase XEEK1, and weaker similarity to many other protein kinases.

relevance_reason: Identifies germline STK11 mutations as the cause of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

findings.statement: Jenne et al. (1998) identified a novel human gene encoding the serine threonine kinase STK11, 190 kb proximal to marker D19S886 in the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome linkage region on 19p13.3. In a 3-generation PJS family, they found an STK11 allele with a deletion of exons 4 and 5 and an inversion of exons 6 and 7 that segregated with the disease.
quotes: In a distance of 190 kb proximal to D19S886, we identified and characterized a novel human gene encoding the serine threonine kinase STK11.
In a three-generation PJ family, we found an STK11 allele with a deletion of exons 4 and 5 and an inversion of exons 6 and 7 segregating with the disease.

variants.as_reported: deletion of exons 4 and 5 and an inversion of exons 6 and 7

findings.statement: By sequence analysis of STK11 exons in 4 unrelated PJS patients, Jenne et al. (1998) identified 3 nonsense mutations and 1 acceptor splice site mutation. All 5 germline mutations found in the study were predicted to disrupt the function of the kinase domain. The authors concluded that germline STK11 mutations, probably in conjunction with acquired defects of the second allele in somatic cells, cause PJS.
quotes: Sequence analysis of STK11 exons in four unrelated PJ patients has identified three nonsense and one acceptor splice site mutations.
All five germline mutations are predicted to disrupt the function of the kinase domain.
We conclude that germline mutations in STK11, probably in conjunction with acquired genetic defects of the second allele in somatic cells, cause the manifestations of PJ syndrome.

findings.statement: Jenne et al. (1998) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by melanocytic macules of the lips, multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps, and an increased risk for various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers (PJ) syndrome is an autosomal-dominant disorder characterized by melanocytic macules of the lips, multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps and an increased risk for various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer.

relevance_reason: Genomewide linkage study in PJS families confirming 19p13.3 locus and suggesting a second locus on 19q13.4.

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) performed a genomewide linkage analysis in 6 PJS families (2 from Spain, 2 from India, 1 from the United States, and 1 from Portugal) comprising 93 individuals, 39 of them affected. Marker D19S886 gave a maximum lod score of 4.74 at theta = 0.045, and multipoint analysis gave a lod score of 7.51 for the interval between D19S886 and 19pter, confirming a PJS locus on 19p13.3.
quotes: using DNA polymorphisms in six families (two from Spain, two from India, one from the United States, and one from Portugal) comprising a total of 93 individuals, including 39 affected and 48 unaffected individuals and 6 individuals with unknown status

marker D19S886 yielded a maximum LOD score of 4.74 at a recombination fraction (theta) of .045; multipoint linkage analysis resulted in a LOD score of 7.51 for the interval between D19S886 and 19 pter

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) found that markers on 19q13.4 also showed significant evidence for linkage in PJS families (maximum lod score of 3.8 at theta = 0.13 for D19S880), mostly contributed by a single family, PJS07. They suggested that a potential second PJS locus on 19q13.4 exists in a minority of families.
quotes: However, markers on 19q13.4 also showed significant evidence for linkage. For example, D19S880 resulted in a maximum LOD score of 3.8 at theta = .13. Most of this positive linkage was contributed by a single family, PJS07.
suggest the existence, in a minority of families, of a potential second PJS locus, on 19q13.4

findings.statement: Mehenni et al. (1997) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as an autosomal dominant disorder with variable expression and incomplete penetrance, characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyposis, with an increased frequency of gastrointestinal and extraintestinal malignancies (ovaries, testes, and breast).
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable expression and incomplete penetrance, characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and hamartomatous polyposis.
Patients with PJS have increased frequency of gastrointestinal and extraintestinal malignancies (ovaries, testes, and breast).

relevance_reason: The paper confirms the earlier mapping of PJS to chromosome 19p and narrows the locus using linkage in five families. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (1997) confirmed linkage of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome to the telomeric region of chromosome 19p and refined the localization of the locus. In the 5 families they examined, there were no recombinants with marker D19S886. The multipoint lod score at D19S886 was 7.52.
quotes: Our studies confirm this location and provide further localization of the PJS locus.
In the five families examined, there were no recombinants with the marker D19S886. The multipoint log odds score at D19S886 is 7.52

findings.statement: Amos et al. (1997) found no evidence for genetic heterogeneity among the 5 Peutz-Jeghers syndrome families they studied.
quotes: we found no evidence for genetic heterogeneity

findings.statement: In the 5 families, Amos et al. (1997) found that all carriers of the at-risk haplotype expressed the Peutz-Jeghers phenotype and no noncarriers showed Peutz-Jeghers sequelae. They concluded that penetrance was complete and that there were no sporadic cases.
quotes: We also found that all carriers expressed the PJS phenotype and no noncarriers displayed PJS sequellae, indicating complete penetrance with no sporadic cases.

relevance_reason: This paper maps the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome susceptibility locus to distal 19p, using CGH and LOH in polyps followed by linkage analysis in 12 families.

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) used comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) of Peutz-Jeghers polyps, together with loss of heterozygosity (LOH) studies, to search for a putative tumor suppressor locus. Linkage analysis in 12 families, using markers from the deletion site, showed a high-penetrance locus in distal 19p. The multipoint lod score was 7.00 at marker D19S886.
quotes: A search for a putative tumour suppressor locus was made using comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) of Peutz-Jeghers polyps, combined with loss of heterozygosity (LOH) study.

Genetic linkage analysis in 12 families using markers from a deletion site demonstrated the presence of a high-penetrance locus in distal 19p with a multipoint lod score of 7.00 at marker D19S886 without evidence of genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: In their linkage analysis of 12 Peutz-Jeghers families, Hemminki et al. (1997) found no evidence of genetic heterogeneity for the distal 19p locus.
quotes: Genetic linkage analysis in 12 families using markers from a deletion site demonstrated the presence of a high-penetrance locus in distal 19p with a multipoint lod score of 7.00 at marker D19S886 without evidence of genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) concluded that their CGH and LOH findings in Peutz-Jeghers polyps pointed to a putative tumor suppressor locus. They also concluded that the findings gave molecular evidence that hamartomas have malignant potential.
quotes: The study demonstrates the power of CGH combined with LOH analysis in identifying putative tumour suppressor loci, and provides molecular evidence of malignant potential in hamartomas.

findings.statement: Hemminki et al. (1997) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as a condition with intestinal hamartomatous polyposis and melanin spots on the lips, buccal mucosa and digits. They noted that a greatly elevated risk of malignancy had been documented, and that gastrointestinal tumors and cancers of the breast, ovary, testis and uterine cervix appear to be overrepresented.
quotes: a condition characterized by intestinal hamartomatous polyposis and melanin spots of the lips, buccal mucosa and digits. A dramatically elevated risk of malignancy has also been documented.
Gastrointestinal tumours as well as cancers of the breast, ovary, testis and uterine cervix appear to be overrepresented in families with this syndrome.

phenotypes.text: melanin spots of lips, buccal mucosa and digits

relevance_reason: Reports a cytogenetic rearrangement (pericentric inversion of chromosome 6) in a patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, with FISH mapping of the breakpoints, as a candidate positional lead.

findings.statement: Markie et al. (1996) found a pericentric inversion of chromosome 6 on karyotype analysis of a patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. They used FISH with YAC clones containing chromosome 6 genetic markers and a centromeric alphoid repeat probe. One inversion breakpoint lay within the alphoid array, in a 1-cM interval between D6S257 and D6S402. The other lay in a 4-cM interval between D6S403 and D6S311. The oestrogen receptor gene locus (ESR) was excluded from the second interval.
quotes: Karyotypic analysis in a patient with Peutz-Jeghers' syndrome demonstrated a pericentric inversion on chromosome 6.
This analysis located one inversion breakpoint within the alphoid array, in a 1-cM interval between D6S257 and D6S402, and the other in a 4-cM interval between D6S403 and D6S311.
The oestrogen receptor gene locus (ESR) is excluded from the latter interval.

relevance_reason: The paper reports feminizing Sertoli cell testicular tumors in 2 boys with probable PJS. It adds clinical, pathologic and biochemical detail on a known feature of the syndrome.

findings.statement: Young et al. (1995) described 2 young boys with probable Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and multicentric Sertoli cell testicular tumors. Both boys had prominent gynecomastia, rapid growth, advanced bone age, and markedly elevated serum estradiol. Serum anti-mullerian hormone, measured in 1 boy, was in the normal range for age. Bilateral orchiectomy was performed in both because the tumor growth would likely cause sterility and continued high estradiol threatened their adult height potential. Four similar cases in boys with PJS had been reported before.
quotes: We report the pathology findings in two cases of multicentric Sertoli cell testicular tumors in two young boys with probable Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Four cases of such tumors occurring in boys with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome were previously reported.
Each of the two boys reported in this paper had prominent gynecomastia, rapid growth, and advanced bone age. Serum levels of estradiol were markedly elevated.

Bilateral orchiectomy was performed in each case because the neoplastic growth would most likely result in sterility, and curtailment of height potential was threatened from continued elevation of estradiol levels.

findings.statement: Under the microscope, the testicular tumors described by Young et al. (1995) consisted of greatly enlarged seminiferous tubules packed with ovoid Sertoli-like cells. A prominent eosinophilic basement membrane surrounded the tubules and extended between the cells, forming hyalinized ovoid globules and microcalcifications. Electron microscopy showed layered basement membranes around adjacent cells and ovoid cells with abundant cytoplasm and limited smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
quotes: Microscopically, greatly enlarged seminiferous tubules packed with ovoid Sertoli-like cells were present. Prominent eosinophilic basement membrane surrounded the tubules and intersected between the cells, forming hyalinized ovoid globules and microcalcifications.
Ultrastructure revealed lamination of basement membranes surrounding adjacent cells, ovoid cells with abundant cytoplasm, and limited smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

findings.statement: Young et al. (1995) found increased transcription of the aromatase cytochrome P450 gene in testicular tumor tissue from both boys with PJS. Transcription used promoter II, the promoter that drives aromatase expression in the normal ovary and testis. Transcript levels were similar to those in corpus luteum, resulting in increased estrogen synthesis. Transcripts from the placental-type aromatase promoters I.1 and I.2 were not detected at significant levels.
quotes: Studies of testicular tumor tissue from both cases revealed increased transcription of the aromatase cytochrome P450 gene using promoter II, the promoter directing aromatase expression in the normal ovary and testis.
The levels of transcripts were comparable to corpus luteum, thus resulting in increased estrogen synthesis.
Transcripts specific for placental-type aromatase promoters (I.1 and I.2) were not detected in significant levels in these tumors.

relevance_reason: Case report of neonatal-onset Peutz-Jeghers syndrome with generalized GI polyposis and early death.

findings.statement: Fernandez Seara et al. (1995) reported a 15-day-old girl with generalized gastrointestinal polyposis resulting from Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Her manifestations included abdominal distention, hematemesis, bloody diarrhea, and edema. She died at 1 year of age of multiple complications of her disease.
quotes: A 15-day-old girl was found to have generalized gastrointestinal polyposis resulting from Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
Her manifestations included abdominal distention, hematemesis, bloody diarrhea, and edema. She died at 1 year of age of multiple complications of her disease.

relevance_reason: Case report of a PJS patient with adenocarcinoma arising in an ileal hamartoma with widespread metastases; adds to the evidence on cancer risk in PJS.

findings.statement: Péloquin et al. (1981) reported a 49-year-old woman with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome whose first symptom was deep thrombophlebitis of the leg, which appeared to be part of a paraneoplastic syndrome. She had an adenocarcinoma that arose in a hamartoma of the terminal ileum, with metastases to the ovary and lymph nodes. Later she developed metastases in the cervical lymph nodes, which responded to chemotherapy for a time.
quotes: the patient, a 49-year-old woman, was first seen with deep thrombophlebitis of the leg which appeared to be part of a paraneoplastic syndrome
The patient had an adenocarcinoma originating in a hamartoma of the terminal ileum, with ovarian and lymph-node metastases.
During the course of the disease the patient was found to have metastatic disease in the cervical lymph nodes which responded, temporarily, to chemotherapy.

phenotypes.text: adenocarcinoma arising in hamartoma of terminal ileum

findings.statement: After reviewing the literature on metastatic Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, Péloquin et al. (1981) concluded that metastatic disease is uncommon, but that all patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome should have close long-term follow-up.
quotes: Although the rate of metastatic disease is low, they believe that all patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome deserve a close long-term follow-up.

relevance_reason: A case report of 3 children who presented with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in early childhood. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Griffith and Bisset (1980) reported 3 cases of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome presenting in early childhood and considered the need for surgical intervention.
quotes: We report 3 cases of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome presenting in early childhood, and consider the need for surgical intervention.

relevance_reason: Family report of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome with bilateral breast cancer and an ovarian SCTAT, supporting an increased tumor risk in PJS.

findings.statement: Riley and Swift (1980) described a family in which the proband and her paternal grandmother both had Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and bilateral breast carcinoma. The proband's breast cancer was premenopausal. When she underwent oophorectomy to treat it, an ovarian sex cord tumor with annular tubules was found incidentally.
quotes: The proband and her paternal grandmother had bilateral breast carcinoma and the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
An ovarian sex cord tumor with annular tubules was an incidental finding when oophorectomy was performed as treatment of the proband's premenopausal breast cancer.

phenotypes.text: ovarian sex cord tumor with annular tubules

findings.statement: Riley and Swift (1980) noted that breast cancer had been reported in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome patients before. They suggested that the Peutz-Jeghers gene may be associated with an increased risk of breast tumors.
quotes: Because there are previous reports of breast cancer in patients with this syndrome, the Peutz-Jeghers gene may be associated with an increased risk of breast tumors.

relevance_reason: This is a clinicopathologic study of a large Peutz-Jeghers family followed for 27 years. It describes jejunal adenocarcinoma arising in a PJ polyp, breast carcinomas, and benign ovarian, breast and thyroid tumors.

findings.statement: Burdick and Prior (1982) followed a family group of 10 patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome for 27 years; 8 family members had 1 or more manifestations of the syndrome. One member died after a bypass procedure for a nonresectable jejunal carcinoma. Postmortem examination showed an adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp, with metastases in the mesenteric lymph nodes.
quotes: A family group of ten patients with the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome has been followed for a 27-year period. Eight members of the family had one or more manifestations of the syndrome.
Postmortem examination revealed this to be an adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp and metastases were present in the mesenteric lymph nodes.

phenotypes.text: adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp

findings.statement: In the family reported by Burdick and Prior (1982), 2 members developed breast carcinoma, 1 of which arose in a fibroadenoma. Both patients died: 1 of metastatic breast carcinoma and the other of a second primary malignancy, an adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp. In addition, 3 family members had benign ovarian tumors, 1 had a benign breast tumor, and 1 had a benign colloid thyroid nodule.
quotes: Two members of the family developed breast carcinomas, one arising in a fibroadenoma; both patients died, one of metastatic breast carcinoma, the other of a second primary malignancy (adenocarcinoma of the jejunum arising in a Peutz-Jeghers polyp).
Three family members had benign ovarian tumors, one patient had a benign breast tumor and another patient had a benign colloid thyroid nodule.

findings.statement: Burdick and Prior (1982) concluded that the exact risk of intestinal cancer in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is unknown but probably very small. They recommended that gastrointestinal surgery continue to be performed in symptomatic patients and that all patients be followed closely at regular intervals.
quotes: the exact risk of intestinal cancer in the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is unknown, but probably very small. Gastrointestinal surgery should continue to be performed in symptomatic patients and all patients should be followed closely at regular intervals.

relevance_reason: The title says the paper is an ultrastructural study of the pigmented macules in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Only the title was available, so no results can be extracted.

findings.statement: Yamada et al. (1981) carried out ultrastructural studies of the pigmented macules of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
quotes: Ultrastructural studies on pigmented macules of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

relevance_reason: Case report of a Peutz-Jeghers syndrome complication: obstructive jaundice caused by a polyp in the common bile duct (title only).

findings.statement: Parker and Knight (1983) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome causing obstructive jaundice due to a polyp in the common bile duct.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome causing obstructive jaundice due to polyp in common bile duct.

relevance_reason: The paper describes Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome: hamartomatous intestinal polyps with macrocephaly and penile café-au-lait spots. This is a different hamartomatous polyposis disorder from Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, so it only gives differential-diagnosis context.

findings.statement: DiLiberti et al. (1983) reported a 7.5-year-old boy with macrocephaly, hamartomatous intestinal polyps, and café-au-lait spots on the penis. They regarded this triad as a new disorder, the Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome, distinct from Sotos syndrome. The authors also considered prominent Schwalbe lines, prominent corneal nerves, and lipid storage myopathy to be part of the syndrome.
quotes: We report on a 7 1/2-year-old boy with macrocephaly, hamartomatous intestinal polyps, and café-au-lait spots on the penis.
We think that this triad of abnormalities represents a new disorder, the Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome.
Prominent Schwalbe lines, prominent corneal nerves, and lipid storage myopathy also appear to be part of the syndrome.

findings.statement: DiLiberti et al. (1983) suggested autosomal dominant inheritance of Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome because the proband's mother had macrocephaly, a similar facial appearance, and a hamartomatous polyp.
quotes: Macrocephaly, similar facial appearance, and a hamartomatous polyp in the mother suggest dominant inheritance.

relevance_reason: This case report describes a boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome who had a feminizing Sertoli cell tumor, adding gonadal tumors to the features of the syndrome.

findings.statement: Cantú et al. (1980) described a 6-year-old boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and a unilateral feminizing Sertoli cell tumor. Histopathologic study of the nontumorous testicular tissue showed changes in the seminiferous tubules. The authors suggested these changes meant that estrogens, directly or indirectly, may have had both stimulating and atrophying effects. They concluded that gonadal tumors are an additional manifestation of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome gene in both male and female patients.
quotes: A case involving a 6-year-old boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and an unilateral feminizing Sertoli cell tumor is described.

The histopathologic studies of nontumorous testicular tissue revealed changes in the seminiferous tubules which suggested that estrogens, directly or indirectly, may have had both stimulating and atrophying effects.
It is concluded that gonadal tumors are in additional manifestation of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome gene in both male and female patients.

findings.statement: In the boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and a feminizing Sertoli cell tumor, Cantú et al. (1980) found consistently high estrogen levels in plasma and urine. Testosterone and dihydrotestosterone levels were normal. Estrogen levels did not change in a way that correlated with administration of exogenous gonadotropin, which the authors took as a sign that estrogen production was autonomous.
quotes: Endocrinologic studies revealed consistently high plasma and urine levels of estrogens and normal levels of testosterone and dihydrotestosterone.
The increased levels of estrogens did not show changes that could be correlated with exogenous gonadotropin administration, thus indicating an autonomous nature.

relevance_reason: The title reports that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome occurred together with precocious puberty. That is a related feature a curator might cite, but only the title was available, so no details can be extracted.

findings.statement: Solh et al. (1983) reported Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with precocious puberty.
quotes: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome associated with precocious puberty.

relevance_reason: Case report of colonic adenocarcinoma in a patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome; relevant to cancer risk in PJS.

findings.statement: Tweedie and McCann (1984) described a 39-year-old man with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome who developed a caecal adenocarcinoma that had metastasized widely to regional lymph nodes. The carcinoma was accompanied by several other colonic Peutz-Jeghers polyps that showed no dysplasia or malignancy, and it could not be determined whether the carcinoma had arisen from a Peutz-Jeghers polyp. The patient also had gastric and small intestinal polyps.
quotes: A case of metastasising colonic carcinoma associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome in a 39 year old man is described.
The caecal adenocarcinoma had metastasised widely to regional lymph nodes and was associated with several other colonic Peutz-Jeghers polyps, showing no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.
The patient also had gastric and small intestinal polyps.

findings.statement: Tweedie and McCann (1984) found that serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) was normal at presentation in their patient with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and metastatic colonic adenocarcinoma, as in one other reported case, and concluded that their report did not support the use of CEA as a screening test in such high-risk groups. They noted that the cancer risk in PJS was unknown and proposed a UK national registry of PJS patients to determine it.
quotes: The serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) was normal at presentation in this patient and in one other reported case.
The use of this determination as a screening test for so-called high risk groups is, therefore, not supported by this report.
A national registry of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome patients in the United Kingdom would help to resolve this question.

quotes: The case of a 6-year-old boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS), gynecomastia, and multifocal and bilateral testicular tumors is described.
This case and other reports from the literature suggest that males, as well as females, with PJS are at risk for developing gonadal tumors.

findings.statement: Giardiello et al. (1987) followed 31 patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome from 1973 to 1985. Cancer, confirmed by histopathologic review, developed in 15 of the 31 (48%): 4 had gastrointestinal carcinomas, 10 had nongastrointestinal carcinomas and 1 had multiple myeloma. Three other patients developed adenomatous polyps of the stomach and colon.
quotes: Cancer developed in 15 of the 31 patients (48 percent)--gastrointestinal carcinomas in 4, nongastrointestinal carcinomas in 10, and multiple myeloma in 1.
In addition, adenomatous polyps of the stomach and colon occurred in three other patients.

findings.statement: Giardiello et al. (1987) found that the cancers were diagnosed when patients were relatively young but after Peutz-Jeghers syndrome had been diagnosed; the interval between the two diagnoses was 25 +/- 20 years (range, 1 to 64). By relative-risk analysis, cancer developed 18 times more often than expected in the general population (P less than 0.0001). The authors suggested that patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome have an increased risk of cancer at both gastrointestinal and nongastrointestinal sites.
quotes: The cancers were diagnosed when the patients were relatively young, but after the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome had been diagnosed (interval between diagnoses, 25 +/- 20 years; range, 1 to 64).
According to relative-risk analysis, the observed development of cancer in the patients with the syndrome was 18 times greater than expected in the general population (P less than 0.0001).

findings.statement: Giardiello et al. (1987) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as an autosomal dominant hereditary disease characterized by hamartomatous polyps of the gastrointestinal tract and mucocutaneous melanin deposits.

findings.statement: Foley et al. (1988) reported 49 years of follow-up of the 'Harrisburg family,' one of the original Peutz-Jeghers families reported by Jeghers. Its 12 affected members made it the largest Peutz-Jeghers kindred reported. Ten patients underwent a total of 75 polypectomies, 1 patient developed short bowel syndrome, and 3 patients died in young adulthood. The authors concluded that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is not a benign disease.
quotes: Of the original Peutz-Jeghers families reported by Jeghers, the "Harrisburg Family" has now been followed for 49 yr. Their 12 affected family members comprise the largest Peutz-Jeghers kindred reported.
Ten patients underwent 75 polypectomies. One patient developed short bowel syndrome. Three patients died in young adulthood.
The course of this family illustrates that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is not a benign disease.

findings.statement: Foley et al. (1988) found that 2 of the 12 affected members of the Harrisburg family developed gastrointestinal malignancy. One of them had a duodenal carcinoma arising in a hamartoma with adenomatous changes, a progression in the duodenum that had not been reported before. The authors suggested that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome may be a premalignant condition.
quotes: One family member developed a duodenal carcinoma in a hamartoma with adenomatous changes; this progression in the duodenum has not previously been reported.
The development of gastrointestinal malignancy in 2 of 12 affected patients suggests that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome may be a premalignant condition.

phenotypes.text: duodenal carcinoma in hamartoma with adenomatous changes

findings.statement: Foley et al. (1988) recommended endoscopic removal of gastric, duodenal, and colonic polyps even when they cause no symptoms. When surgery is needed, they suggested intraoperative endoscopy with polypectomy to help prevent short bowel syndrome. They also proposed that colonoscopic screening of patients and their family members may be beneficial and that surveillance for extraintestinal malignancy appeared to be warranted.
quotes: Consequently, even asymptomatic gastric, duodenal, and colonic polyps should be removed endoscopically. If surgical intervention is necessary, intraoperative endoscopy with polypectomy may prevent the development of a short bowel syndrome.
Colonoscopic screening of patients and their family members may be beneficial and surveillance for extraintestinal malignancy appears to be warranted.

findings.statement: Spigelman et al. (1989) reported that malignant tumors developed in 16 (22%) of 72 patients with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, and all but 1 of these 16 patients died. Nine of the tumors were gastrointestinal and 7 were nongastrointestinal. The relative risk of death was 13 (95% CI 2.7-38.1) from gastrointestinal cancer and 9 (95% CI 4.2-17.3) from all cancers. The chance of dying of cancer by age 57 years was 48%.
quotes: Among 72 patients with the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome malignant tumours have developed in 16 (22%) of whom all but one have died.
There were nine gastrointestinal and seven nongastrointestinal tumours.
The relative risks of death from gastrointestinal cancer and all cancers were 13 (95% CI 2.7-38.1) and 9 (95% CI 4.2-17.3) respectively. The chance of dying of cancer by the age of 57 was 48%.

findings.statement: In the 4 patients with Laugier-Hunziker syndrome, Veraldi et al. Ultrastructural study showed the presence of numerous mature melanosomes in the cytoplasm of the keratinocytes of the basal layer and of the melanophages in the papillary dermis. Alterations of the melanocytes were not observed.
